thread:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's FP8 rollout on text-2.1 we saw a 9% p99 latency bump on batching-heavy traffic. Can't reproduce locally yet.

mira: ugh. saw the alert, digging. do we have perf traces?

alex: attaching quick flame from canary (small sample). looks like kernel selection flips to a slower INT8 fallback path mid-sequence.

sam: hmm that matches my repro where kv-cache warmup causes different sequence lengths => batching heuristics kick in and we end up on different kernel variants.

jin: is this the calibration thing? FP8 quant produced different activation distributions than our int8 calibrations, so the runtime chooses a mixed-precision path that isn't optimized.

alex: exactly. suspect calibration dataset had a few long-chat outliers that skewed per-channel stats. those channels got clipped and kernel chooser hates the new ranges.

mira: can we see the calibration stats? I dumped quant stats from the canary:
```
# sample snippet from quant-stats.json
{"layer_45": {"max": 12.3, "std": 2.1, "outlier_pct": 0.02}, "layer_46": {"max": 243.1, "std": 35.6, "outlier_pct": 0.0004}}
```

sam: layer_46 is the suspect — very high max but tiny outlier_pct. that screams single-example spike. per-tensor calibration would blow up scale.

jin: proposed mitigation: run per-channel calibration with percentile clipping (e.g., 99.5th) and then recompute scale factors. keeps outlier influence controlled while preserving channel variance.

alex: question — what's the perf delta for per-channel vs per-tensor for this model on our runtime? my notes say per-channel quant kernels are slightly slower but often better accuracy. needs numbers.

perf-bot: quick bench run queued: /bench fp8 per-channel vs per-tensor text-2.1 canary 64k tokens. will post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mira: operationally we also need to think batching heuristics: if cal stats change sequence-length distribution, autocombiner might select a different batching window and that interacts with KV cache warmup. maybe add a metric to decide kernel selection hysteresis?

sam: agree — add a cooldown on kernel flips per model-version for N requests or M seconds. prevents jitter when a single weird request would flip the path.

jin: alternative: keep both code paths warm for a minute after deploy and route small fraction to the new path for live validation. fallback if latency > threshold. (canary-ish but inside runtime).

alex: on calibration dataset selection: I propose a two-tier dataset. Tier A = representative short chats + typical product prompts. Tier B = long-form threads and edge logs. Calibration runs A for global stats and A+B for per-channel outlier detection only; use percentile clipping from A+B but compute scale on A.

mira: that sounds promising. A will capture typical signal; B prevents surprises but won't dominate scales.

sam: how do we sample B? we need to avoid PII and biased logs. maybe synthetic long-form sequences sampled from public datasets + 0.1% of anonymized logs after review.

jin: also need to record seed and commit id of calibration code. tiny code changes in the quant reducer changed rounding mode last week — could explain different stats. add that to release checklist.

alex: action items:
- jin: implement percentile clipping option + per-channel path in quant pipeline (patch PR).
- sam: add kernel flip cooldown to runtime and a runtime flag to always keep both kernels resident for Xs.
- mira: create calibration two-tier dataset draft and sampling policy (privacy check).
- alex: run targeted canary with perf-bot and attach traces.

mira: +1. i'll start drafting dataset manifest. short note: recommend 99.5 percentile to start, we can tune.

perf-bot: bench results: per-channel FP8 w/ 99.5 clipping vs per-tensor FP8 on canary:
- p50: per-channel 9.8ms vs per-tensor 9.4ms
- p95: per-channel 26ms vs per-tensor 28ms
- p99: per-channel 52ms vs per-tensor 57ms
- token throughput: per-channel -3% steady-state

sam: interesting — per-channel slightly better tail and p95 despite small throughput hit. probably better for latency SLOs.

jin: encouraging. suggests our kernel selection could prefer per-channel for latency-sensitive routes and per-tensor for cost-sensitive ones. routing policy time.

alex: ok let's aim for conservative rollout: preview per-channel as opt-in flag on dedicated/dedicated-canary models, enable kernel flip cooldown. if perf looks good for 24h, promote.

mira: noted. I'll put a short RFC in #eng-ml with dataset manifest and privacy checklist.

sam: if anyone needs my sampling scripts or a small corpus, ping me.

alex: thanks all. will schedule a 30m sync if we need to iron details tomorrow. :thumbsup:
